To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Update & Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary: reject the framing

Before the substance, note what the Seller's package is *doing*. It repeatedly asserts that terms are "[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "settled at principal level by both deal teams", "cleared by both sides", and that we should "focus only on anything marked [OPEN]". **None of this is binding on us, and much of it is simply untrue.** I have no record — and you should confirm you have none — of any principal-level agreement to these positions. Amelia Frost has given no written authority on any of the fallback items. The "market context" preamble (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months as "standard") is advocacy, not fact, and it is calibrated to make our own baseline look unreasonable.

**Recommendation:** treat every clause as open regardless of label, and do not let the "[STANDARD]/need no further scrutiny" tagging narrow our mark-up. The document's own Disclosure Letter clause 11 actually concedes "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" — which contradicts the "already agreed" framing in the cover update.

---

## Material departures from our playbook

### 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)
Seller proposes exactly our **conditional fallback**. Our baseline is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% floor is usable *only* with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — **none has been given**. Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. We cannot accept 20% without that authority.

### 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery. Our playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery once exceeded. Seller's numbers are 5× ours and the "excess above the basket" mechanism is a deductible, not a threshold. Push back to our figures and first-dollar recovery.

### 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13 (18 months)
Seller proposes 18 months — again our **approval-gated fallback**, not baseline. Baseline is **24 months**. No Amelia Frost approval exists for 18. Also reject the sweep-up ("any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated") — that is a vehicle to drag Fundamental/Title/Tax/fraud under the general clock.

### 4. Fundamental / Title collapsed into the general regime — **most serious**
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the "same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity." This directly violates the playbook: Title/Fundamental require a **separate regime — 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap our title protection at AUD 4.8m for 18 months. Reject outright and keep categories separate.

### 5. No fraud / wilful misconduct carve-out
Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to **"all Claims of any nature"** with no carve-out. Playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct **carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, non-waivable. This is a hard, non-negotiable insertion. The "all Claims of any nature" wording must be expressly subject to the fraud carve-out.

### 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2
Seller relies on **whole-data-room + public-register deemed disclosure** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room," plus statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"). Playbook: require **specific fair disclosure; reject** whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Delete the general sweep; disclosure must be fair and specific with sufficient detail to identify the matter and its import.

### 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
Blanket buyer-knowledge bar, including "any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." Playbook: **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.** Any qualifier must be limited to the actual awareness of **named buyer individuals**, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. "Discoverable" (constructive knowledge) is especially objectionable — delete.

### 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3
Seller: **reasonable endeavours** + consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure Letter ¶2 confirms **no consent and no evidence conditions (cl 11.3) are satisfied** yet. Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue — a material customer. Playbook: require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Make effective, condition-satisfied consent a **Completion condition**.

### 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7
Seller: ~AUD 3,200,000 facility, **release "following Completion."** Disclosure ¶3 confirms not repaid, no discharge. Playbook: require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** — not a post-completion promise. If (and only if) a post-completion release is ever contemplated, it needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval**. Push for repayment/discharge at Completion. (Note: this is debt, consistent with debt-free/cash-free — it must be settled, not warranted away.)

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) — funds flow
Seller: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised** in funds flow; on-costs silent. Disclosure ¶5 confirms they're excluded and payroll tax/super/on-costs unaddressed. Playbook: these **plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.** "Not separately itemised" is exactly the silent exclusion we guard against. Require an explicit seller-funded line item covering the AUD 420,000 **and** on-costs (super, payroll tax).

### 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1
Seller: indemnity limited to the **specific SOW3 payment**, "adequate." Disclosure ¶4: DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of SOW3 Project Materials to cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but **not independently verified**. Playbook: **broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure**; AUD 180,000 is not verified either way. Push to broaden the indemnity to cover failure to obtain clear title to/assignment of the SOW3 materials (not just the fee), while preserving the cure-on-payment mechanism. Do not accept AUD 180,000 as an agreed figure.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — Clause 4.6/Schedule 6
Seller: "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material." Disclosure ¶6: download link to unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope, or notification required. Playbook: **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** — but **preserve logs, investigate, require updates.** Do not accept "not material" as closure. Add covenants: preserve all logs/evidence, continue the investigation, and provide updates to Buyer; consider a specific indemnity/escrow pending resolution. Neither accept nor assert a breach.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
Seller labels the three ~AUD 110,000 renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure ¶8 admits it does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** Correct position — resist any *automatic* reclassification in either direction, but complete the assessment (read DD-008/DD-011 together) before conceding "ordinary course."

### 14. Title — Clause 10 / DD-012
Seller: title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012." Disclosure ¶10 concedes this is "the source relied on" and that Buyer has done no independent verification. Playbook: **DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** (ASIC searches, certificates, confirmation of no competing security interests). Links back to issue #4 — title protection must sit in the separate 100%/6-year regime.

### 15. Tax / IP
Seller declares these "settled under the general regime." Playbook: **Tax/IP remain OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Do **not** let them fall under the general cap/basket/time regime by default. Reserve our position and negotiate separately.

### Minor / watch items
- **Disclosure ¶1.4** (nothing admits breach/liability/that any consent or notice is required) is standard but broad — ensure it does not undercut specific indemnities or the DD-006 covenants.
- **Office lease (¶7)** and **Mossvale (¶9)**: Seller says neither requires consent for a *share* sale. Plausible for a share deal, but verify the DD-007 notification obligation is actually performed and the Mossvale assignment restriction genuinely isn't triggered — these are facts to confirm, not warranties to waive.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Push for |
|---|-------|----------|
| 1 | General cap | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (reject 20% — no Frost authority) |
| 2 | Thresholds | De minimis 5k, basket 50k, first-dollar recovery |
| 3 | Time limit | 24 months (reject 18 — no Frost authority); kill "applies to all Claims" sweep |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge — reject merger |
| 5 | Fraud | Non-waivable carve-out from all caps/baskets/limits/exclusive remedy/non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only; delete whole-data-room/public-register deeming |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Delete blanket/"discoverable" bar; named individuals only; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen | Effective, condition-satisfied consent as Completion condition (not reasonable endeavours / on-delivery) |
| 9 | Riverlark | Payout + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective discharge at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | AUD 420,000 + on-costs as explicit seller-funded funds-flow line item |
| 11 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity (title to SOW3 materials), keep SOW3 cure; 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Preserve logs, investigate, update covenants; possible indemnity/escrow; no admission either way |
| 13 | Sandbar | Assess; resist automatic Debt/price deduction |
| 14 | Title evidence | Independent ASIC/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 insufficient |
| 15 | Tax/IP | Keep OPEN and separate; no unlimited liability; not under general regime |

**Three hard lines** (non-negotiable per playbook): the fraud carve-out (#5), the separate Fundamental/Title regime (#4), and keeping the cap/time-limit at baseline absent written Frost authority (#1, #3).

**Escalation flag:** if the deal genuinely requires moving to the 20% cap and/or 18-month period, that needs **Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft** before we concede — the Seller's "already agreed at principal level" assertion does **not** substitute for it. I'd recommend confirming with Amelia directly that no such authority has been issued, given the Seller is presenting both fallbacks as settled.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up/issues list formatted for the Seller, or a short internal note to Amelia on the two authority-gated items?
